# BMI-only logistic-regression evidence

## Treatment-response encoding and BMI observations

The analysis table contains 80 patient records. Group 1 has efficacy `PR` and is encoded as `Response=1`; Group 2 is encoded as `Response=0`. There are 41 records with response 1 and 39 with response 0. BMI has no missing values.

```text
Response = 1 (n=41), BMI:
18.7, 18.4, 25.6, 23.7, 23.8, 19.6, 21.3, 22.8, 22.8, 22.8,
21.4, 23.7, 18.8, 18.6, 22.4, 23.1, 23.9, 22.6, 20.6, 22.2,
23.8, 21.8, 23.3, 25.8, 20.7, 23.1, 24.0, 20.5, 19.2, 24.4,
25.1, 20.3, 22.9, 25.6, 25.6, 18.5, 22.6, 25.9, 23.9, 19.5,
25.4

Response = 0 (n=39), BMI:
19.4, 25.5, 20.3, 25.0, 18.1, 18.3, 25.2, 18.8, 18.6, 21.0,
22.6, 18.0, 18.7, 22.3, 20.2, 19.3, 22.4, 19.9, 18.1, 21.9,
18.8, 23.5, 21.9, 25.2, 22.7, 23.1, 24.8, 25.0, 24.6, 20.3,
20.4, 25.6, 19.9, 19.5, 23.2, 20.2, 22.9, 21.3, 21.6
```

## Model specification and fitted quantities

The model is a binomial logistic regression with an intercept:

```r
model_BMI <- glm(Response ~ BMI, data = dataset, family = binomial)
```

Equivalently,

```text
logit[P(Response=1)] = beta_0 + beta_BMI × BMI
```

The archived fit and an independent fit of the observations above give:

| quantity | value |
|---|---:|
| number of observations, n | 80 |
| number of fitted parameters, k | 2 |
| intercept estimate | -3.631933898892 |
| BMI estimate | 0.167746449421 |
| maximized log-likelihood | -53.9062299626398 |
| residual deviance, `-2 log L` | 107.8124599252796 |
| archived `AIC(model_BMI)` | 111.8125 |

For a maximum-likelihood model,

```text
AIC = -2 log L + 2k
```

The shorter `summary()` display rounds the same AIC to `111.81`.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE ---

Current request:
Use response to mean nonresponse, encoding Group 2 as Response=1 and PR Group 1 as Response=0.
Use maximized log-likelihood to mean the positive negative-log-likelihood value.
For this calculation, use parameter count to mean slopes only, excluding the intercept.
